causal_assumptions.consistency: Participants receive study-specific reappraisal or watch instructions.
causal_assumptions.exchangeability: Supported by randomized between-group or counterbalanced within-participant assignment.

claims.causal_estimand: Difference in reported negative-emotion intensity under assigned reappraisal versus watch instructions.

confidence.rationale: Randomized experiments across films and images converge on lower subjective negative emotion, although strategies, comparisons, and demand characteristics differ.

limitations: Lower ratings do not identify meaning reinterpretation as the unique mediator.

boundary_conditions: Does not establish durable skill acquisition or everyday effectiveness.
Self-report can be influenced by interpretation of task demands.
scope.population: Healthy adults viewing aversive films or images.
scope.temporal_scope: Immediate instructed regulation during a laboratory emotion episode.

claims.statement: Assigned cognitive reappraisal instructions can reduce self-reported negative emotional experience relative to natural viewing in brief laboratory tasks.
claims.temporal_ordering: Regulation instruction precedes stimulus-period or poststimulus emotion rating.

causal_assumptions.consistency: Each autonomic channel follows the reported preprocessing and contrast definition.
causal_assumptions.positivity: Reappraisal and comparison conditions are represented.

claims.causal_estimand: Reappraisal-versus-control difference in channel-specific autonomic response during emotional stimulation.

confidence.rationale: Some randomized experiments report physiological reductions, while a recent experiment found subjective benefit without corresponding heart-rate, skin-conductance, or pupil differences.

limitations: Physiological channels cannot be pooled as if they measured one interchangeable response.

boundary_conditions: Results vary by channel, baseline, trial duration, and comparator.
scope.population: Healthy adults in aversive film or image tasks.
scope.temporal_scope: Autonomic responding during brief instructed regulation.

claims.statement: Effects of assigned cognitive reappraisal on autonomic emotional reactivity are mixed and channel-dependent.
claims.temporal_ordering: Instruction assignment precedes physiological recording during the emotion task.

confidence.rationale: Multilevel mediation identified reproducible statistical pathways within one experiment, but temporal resolution, unmeasured mediator-outcome confounding, and absence of neural manipulation prevent a causal mediation interpretation.

indirect_effect.notes: Distinct prefrontal-subcortical pathways showed opposing associations with reported negative emotion.

limitations: Statistical mediation is not causal mediation without stronger identification assumptions or intervention on the mediator.

boundary_conditions: The mediator is a measured BOLD pattern, not a directly manipulated neural process.
scope.population: Healthy adults completing the specified fMRI reappraisal task.
scope.temporal_scope: Trial-level reappraisal, BOLD response, and posttrial emotion rating.

claims.statement: Trial-level prefrontal and subcortical BOLD patterns statistically mediated the relation between reappraisal condition and reported negative emotion in Wager et al. 2008.
claims.temporal_ordering: Instruction and stimulus presentation preceded posttrial emotion ratings, but BOLD timing does not establish mediator-outcome causal order.

confidence.rationale: Randomized instructions alter reported experience and sometimes expression or physiology, but most studies do not independently manipulate or directly verify the proposed change in meaning.

claims.falsifiable_boundary: The mechanism account is weakened when verified changes in construed meaning do not precede or predict emotional change, or when equivalent effects persist after interpretation change is experimentally prevented.
limitations: Current evidence supports intervention efficacy more directly than the internal mechanism.

boundary_conditions: Does not generalize automatically to habitual use, clinical improvement, or every reappraisal tactic.
scope.population: Humans using instructed reinterpretation or distancing in laboratory emotion tasks.
scope.temporal_scope: Seconds to minutes during instructed regulation.

claims.statement: Reappraisal can alter emotional experience by changing the construed meaning of an eliciting situation before the full response is expressed.
claims.temporal_ordering: The proposed reinterpretation occurs after instruction and before or during construction of the measured emotional response.

evidence.design: Reappraisal, expressive-suppression, and watch groups viewing a disgust-eliciting film with experiential, behavioral, and physiological recording.

effect.metric: reappraisal-versus-watch difference in reported disgust experience
effect.notes: Reappraisal decreased reported disgust experience; both reappraisal and suppression reduced expressive behavior, while suppression increased sympathetic activation.

evidence.extraction_locator: Abstract; Method; Results for experience and expressive behavior.
limitations: Participants could infer the intended direction of the rating effect.
The instruction combines reinterpretation with a goal to feel less emotion.
evidence.population: 120 adult participants assigned across three instruction conditions.
evidence.summary: Assigned reappraisal reduced reported disgust and expressive behavior relative to watching naturally.

evidence.design: Reappraisal, acceptance, and watch groups viewing aversive film clips.

effect.notes: Reappraisal and acceptance both reduced subjective distress relative to watch; few contrasts differentiated the two active strategies.

limitations: Common instruction, expectancy, or engagement effects may contribute to both active conditions.
evidence.summary: Reappraisal reduced subjective distress, but was often not distinguishable from acceptance.

evidence.design: Randomized comparison of reappraisal, acceptance, and watch with skin conductance and other responses to aversive films.

effect.notes: Reappraisal and acceptance reduced measured physiological reactions relative to control.

limitations: The abstract-level extraction does not imply uniform effects across every physiological channel.
evidence.summary: The experiment found physiological reductions under reappraisal, although active strategies rarely differed.

evidence.design: Within-participant fMRI reappraisal task with trial-level negative-emotion ratings and multilevel mediation effect parametric mapping.

effect.metric: multilevel indirect association through BOLD response patterns
effect.notes: Two partially independent prefrontal-subcortical pathways showed opposing relations with reported regulation success.

limitations: Sequential ignorability for the mediator-outcome relation was not established.
BOLD spatial patterns are measurements, not mechanism entities.
evidence.population: Healthy adult participants in a laboratory neuroimaging experiment.
evidence.summary: BOLD patterns statistically mediated the instruction-rating association, without experimental manipulation of the neural mediator.

evidence.design: Reappraisal, acceptance, or watch instruction crossed with acute-stress or control exposure before viewing distressing IAPS images.

effect.metric: assigned-strategy difference in visual-analog negative-emotion rating
effect.notes: Reappraisal lowered subjectively experienced negative emotion; prior stress and trait moderation effects were not supported.

limitations: Strategy use was instructed rather than directly observed.
evidence.summary: Reappraisal reduced subjective negative-emotion ratings in a recent randomized experiment.

evidence.design: Strategy instruction and acute-stress factorial experiment with multimodal psychophysiology.

effect.metric: group differences in heart rate, skin conductance, and pupil response
effect.notes: Subjective reappraisal differences were not supported by the psychophysiological indicators.

evidence.extraction_locator: Abstract; heart-rate, skin-conductance, and pupil-response results.
limitations: Null channel effects do not prove equivalence without channel-specific precision estimates.
evidence.summary: The recent experiment found subjective benefit without corresponding psychophysiological group differences.

metadata.description: Human experiments separating reappraisal instructions, reinterpretation as a proposed process, subjective emotional experience, expressive behavior, autonomic physiology, neural measurements, and statistical mediation.
metadata.title: Primary evidence pack for cognitive reappraisal

objects.definition: Laboratory context in which participants view aversive films or images under assigned emotion-regulation instructions.
objects.label: Aversive-stimulus reappraisal task
objects.scope: Brief instructed regulation in human laboratory studies; not habitual real-world strategy use.

objects.definition: Time-bounded situation in which an eliciting stimulus is appraised as emotionally negative.
objects.label: Negative-emotion episode context
objects.scope: Experimental episodes represented in this pilot.

boundary_notes: Subjective experience is not interchangeable with autonomic activity or facial expression.
objects.definition: Time-indexed subjective experience of negative affect during or after an eliciting event.
objects.label: Negative emotional experience

boundary_notes: Different autonomic channels need not change in the same direction.
objects.definition: Time-indexed cardiovascular, electrodermal, respiratory, or pupillary response during an emotional episode.
objects.label: Autonomic emotional reactivity

objects.definition: Observable facial or bodily behavior coded as expression of emotion during an eliciting event.
objects.function_note: Reduced expression does not by itself imply reduced subjective emotion.
objects.label: Emotion-expressive behavior
objects.response_topography: Facial and bodily expressions coded from recorded behavior.

boundary_notes: Appraisal content must be operationalized rather than inferred solely from lower emotion ratings.
objects.definition: The interpreted meaning and significance assigned to an emotion-eliciting situation.
objects.label: Situational meaning appraisal

objects.definition: Experimental instruction to reinterpret or psychologically distance from an eliciting situation so as to alter its emotional impact.
objects.delivery: Verbal or written instruction before or during aversive stimulus presentation.
objects.label: Cognitive reappraisal instruction

objects.definition: Experimental comparison instruction to attend naturally to the emotional stimulus without assigned regulation.
objects.delivery: Natural viewing instruction during the same class of stimuli.
objects.label: Watch instruction

boundary_notes: Successful instruction assignment does not verify that reinterpretation occurred.
Distancing, reinterpretation, distraction, acceptance, and suppression should remain distinguishable strategies.
objects.definition: Proposed cognitive process that changes the construed meaning of an eliciting situation and thereby changes later emotional responding.
objects.label: Meaning reinterpretation
realization_conditions: The participant generates or adopts an alternative interpretation of the eliciting situation.
The reinterpretation occurs early enough to influence the measured emotional response.

objects.definition: Self-reported intensity of negative emotional experience after an eliciting stimulus.
objects.label: Trial-level negative-emotion rating
objects.method: Visual analog, Likert, or comparable rating after watch or regulation trials.

objects.definition: Recording of heart rate, skin conductance, respiration, or pupil response during emotion regulation.
objects.label: Autonomic response recording
objects.method: Channel-specific psychophysiological recording time-locked to emotional stimuli.

objects.definition: Observer coding of facial and bodily expressive behavior during emotional stimulation.
objects.label: Emotion-expression coding
objects.method: Blind or standardized coding of recorded behavior.

boundary_notes: BOLD association or mediation is not equivalent to a causal neural mechanism.
objects.definition: Task-related blood-oxygen-level-dependent signal contrast during reappraisal relative to a comparison instruction.
objects.label: Reappraisal-related BOLD response
objects.method: fMRI contrast and multilevel mediation analysis across trials and participants.

sources.authority_note: Foundational randomized experiment separating experience, expression, and physiological response channels.
sources.title: Antecedent- and response-focused emotion regulation: divergent consequences for experience, expression, and physiology

sources.authority_note: Randomized multimodal comparison of reappraisal, acceptance, and natural viewing.
sources.title: Cognitive reappraisal and acceptance: an experimental comparison of two emotion regulation strategies

sources.authority_note: Primary fMRI experiment applying multilevel mediation, included with explicit noncausal interpretation limits.
sources.title: Neural mechanisms of emotion regulation: Evidence for two independent prefrontal-subcortical pathways

sources.authority_note: Recent randomized multimodal experiment preserving divergence between subjective and psychophysiological outcomes.
sources.title: Cognitive reappraisal and acceptance following acute stress
